# Bookmark Feature Requirements Checklist: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

**Purpose**: Validate the quality (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage) of
spec.md's requirements for the chat-message bookmark feature — the four-state control, its save/idempotency
behavior, its error resilience, and its scoping to user-only messages — before implementation proceeds.
**Created**: 2026-10-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item
`[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied — not when the
underlying implementation behavior has been verified.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It
does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Bookmark State Machine Completeness & Clarity

- [ ] CHK001 Are all four bookmark states (`idle`, `saving`, `saved`, `error`) and every permitted transition
  between them fully enumerated, with no transition left implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/FR-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the claim that the `saved` state is terminal and non-interactive stated precisely enough to
  rule out an alternate reading where a visibly `saved` bookmark could still be tapped? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the requirements for what happens when a bookmark is in `saving` and receives another tap
  (ignored vs. queued vs. erroring) unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the requirement for re-entering `saving` from `error` on retry distinguished clearly enough
  from the first-ever `idle → saving` transition, so a reader cannot conflate "first save" and "retry" as
  needing different backend calls? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, US3]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec define what state a bookmark must render in in the window before the client has
  determined whether a given message was already saved (e.g., immediately after a conversation loads)?
  [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Duplicate-Prevention & Idempotency Requirement Quality

- [ ] CHK006 Is "the existing entry is reused" (rather than a new entry being created) stated as an
  observable, testable outcome rather than only as an internal implementation goal? [Measurability, Spec
  §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the two distinct duplicate-risk scenarios — a literal re-tap on an already-`saved` control,
  and a save retried with no local record of a prior success — both covered by requirements, and is the
  boundary between them (one is a non-event because `saved` is non-interactive, the other is the real
  idempotency path) unambiguous? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, US2]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the source of the duplicate-prevention guarantee (backend idempotency vs. a client-side
  mechanism) stated clearly enough that a reader would not design a redundant client-side dedup check against
  the requirements alone? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements defined for what the bookmark must display while duplicate-safety is being
  resolved (i.e., a retried save against an already-saved message), so the UI outcome during that window is
  specified and not just the end state? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]

## Error & Offline Resilience Requirement Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Are all distinct failure causes called out in the spec (no connection, timeout, other write
  failure, post-write pipeline failure) required to produce the same observable `error` state, or does the
  spec leave room for cause-specific UI that isn't otherwise defined? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "MUST NOT block, delay, or otherwise affect any other part of the chat screen" quantified or
  made objectively verifiable, or does it rely on a reader's subjective judgment of what counts as "affect"?
  [Measurability, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements defined for the bookmark's state when a save is in flight and the user
  navigates away and back before it resolves, covering both eventual outcomes (success and failure)? [Edge
  Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec define bookmark behavior requirements for the session-expiry overlay scenario in
  enough detail to be independently verifiable (e.g., what the bookmark shows immediately after
  re-authentication), or only the qualitative claim that it is "not stuck"? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements for a save failing at/near the content length limit specific enough to
  distinguish "succeeds normally" from "surfaces a backend validation error as the error state," or could a
  reader implement only one of the two outcomes and still believe they satisfied the requirement? [Clarity,
  Spec §Edge Cases]

## Message-Scoping Requirement Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Is "every user message" scoped precisely enough to state whether it includes messages in every
  delivery/status condition (sending, failed-to-send, optimistic/not-yet-confirmed), or is that left to
  inference? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the named exceptions ("insight cards," "partial/failed assistant responses") sufficient to
  cover every assistant-rendered UI element the chat screen can produce, or could an unlisted assistant-side
  element exist that the requirement doesn't explicitly exclude? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the spec define requirements for a message whose authorship is ambiguous or system-
  generated (neither a clear user message nor a clear assistant response), or is that case assumed not to
  exist without being stated? [Gap, Assumption]

## Cross-Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK018 Are the `occurredAt`/timestamp requirements (entry dated to the message's own send time, not the
  tap time) consistent between the Assumptions section and every acceptance scenario that describes a saved
  entry's content? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the requirement that chat-sourced entries be "structurally indistinguishable" from RF01
  entries (US1, Scenario 3) consistent with FR-003's requirement that `source` and `chatMessageId` always
  differ for chat-sourced entries, without one requirement implicitly contradicting the other's intent? [Consistency, Spec §US1, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the shared entry-creation interface requirement (FR-009) stated with enough precision to be
  checked against the spec alone (e.g., "same use case," not "same effect"), given that the exact contract
  shape is explicitly deferred to planning? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria & Success Criteria Measurability

- [ ] CHK021 Can SC-001 through SC-005 each be evaluated as pass/fail using only information available from
  the spec, without requiring an implementer's own interpretation of an undefined term? [Measurability, Spec
  §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK022 Does SC-005's qualifier ("where the client has a way to know the save already succeeded") risk
  making the success criterion unfalsifiable, or is the boundary of "has a way to know" defined elsewhere in
  the spec precisely enough to make the criterion testable? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and
  `/speckit-clarify` — this file is a distinct, custom checklist and does not replace it.

452	
453	### Phase Dependencies
454	
455	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
456	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup — BLOCKS all user stories.
457	- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: Depends on Foundational. Delivers the MVP end-to-end.
458	- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: Depends on Foundational *and* on User Story 1's `_onBookmarkTapped`/
459	  `BookmarkButton` (T019/T021/T024) existing to verify against — it adds no new production code.
460	- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: Same — depends on Foundational and US1's T019/T021/T024, adds no new production
461	  code.
462	- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: Depends on Foundational and US1's T022/T023, adds no new production code.
463	- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four user stories being complete.
464	
465	### Within Each Phase
466	
467	- Foundational: T004 gates T005/T006/T007 (all three extend callers of the interface T004 changes); T009/T010
468	  are independent of each other and of T002-T008, but T011 needs both.
469	- User Story 1: T014/T015 (event/state shapes) gate T016 (bloc wiring), which gates T017→T018→T019→T020. T021
470	  (widget) is independent of the bloc chain and only needs T002/T003; T022 needs T021; T023 needs T022 and
471	  T014. Tests T024-T026 need their respective implementation tasks done first.
472	- User Stories 2-4: each task lists its own single prerequisite from Foundational/US1 above; tasks within a
473	  phase are otherwise independent of each other.
474	
475	### Parallel Opportunities
476	
477	- All of T002, T003, T009, T010 (Foundational) can run in parallel — four different files, no shared
478	  dependency.
479	- T005, T006, T007 can run in parallel once T004 is done.
480	- T012 and T013 (chat-repository tests) can run in parallel once T011 is done.
481	- In User Story 1, T021 (the `BookmarkButton` widget) can be built in parallel with T014-T020 (the bloc/event/
482	  state chain) — they only converge at T022.
483	- Every `[P]`-marked test task within US2/US3/US4 can run in parallel with its siblings in the same phase.
484	
485	---

487	## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase
488	
489	```bash
490	# Launch together — four independent files:
491	Task: "Create BookmarkStatus enum in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_status.dart"
492	Task: "Add sizeBookmarkIcon/spacingBookmarkGap to lib/core/design_tokens.dart"
493	Task: "Add chatSavedMessageEntryIds key to lib/features/chat/data/chat_local_cache.dart"
494	Task: "Add savedEntryIdFor/recordMessageSaved to lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart"
495	
496	# Once the EntriesRepository interface (T004) is extended, launch together:
497	Task: "Extend CreateEntryUseCase.call with chatMessageId/occurredAt"
498	Task: "Extend EntriesRepositoryImpl.create to pass the two params through"
499	Task: "Extend EntriesRemoteDataSource.create to add the two fields to the request body"
500	```
501	
502	---
503	
504	## Implementation Strategy
505	
506	### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)
507	
508	1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
509	2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (blocks everything).
510	3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 — tap a message, get a persisted, restart-safe entry.
511	4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: run quickstart.md Story 1 manually; this is already a demoable, shippable increment.
512	
513	### Incremental Delivery
514	
515	1. Setup + Foundational → shared plumbing ready.
516	2. User Story 1 → the MVP: save, persist, survive restart.
517	3. User Story 2 → verify the duplicate-prevention guarantee US1's own code already provides.
518	4. User Story 3 → verify failure isolation/retry US1's own code already provides.
519	5. User Story 4 → verify the user-only placement US1's own code already provides by construction.
520	6. Polish → coverage/lint/architecture gates, FR-010 scope check.
521	
522	Unlike a typical feature where each story adds new code, US2-US4 here are deliberately verification-only
523	phases: the single `_onBookmarkTapped` handler and `ChatMessageBubble`/`BookmarkButton` composition built in
524	US1 already satisfy FR-004 (dedup), FR-005/FR-006/FR-007 (failure isolation), and FR-001 (user-only placement)
525	by construction (per spec.md's own Assumptions and research.md R6/R8/R9/R10) — so their phases schedule the
526	tests and manual checks that prove it, not new production code.
527	
528	---
529	
530	## Notes
531	
532	- `[P]` tasks touch different files with no dependency on an incomplete task in the same phase.
533	- `[Story]` labels trace every task back to spec.md's own four user stories.
534	- Tests are included per contract scenario table (`contracts/*.md`) — run them and confirm they pass, not just
535	  that they exist.
536	- Commit after each task or logical group.
537	- Stop at any checkpoint to validate a story independently before moving on.

# Tasks: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/008-chat-message-bookmark/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md — all present and read.

**Tests**: Included. The Testing section of plan.md and the RNF07 (≥80% domain coverage)/RNF09 (15/15 error
scenarios) gates `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks "PASS (gate carried into tasks)" make test coverage a
project requirement for this unit, not optional polish. Every contract's own scenario table
(`contracts/*.md`) is scheduled below against the test file it belongs in.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (spec.md's four, in priority order: US1/US2 both P1, US3/US4
both P2). Foundational tasks build the shared plumbing (enum, tokens, the extended `CreateEntryUseCase` seam,
the device-local "already saved" record) every story depends on but that is not itself a user-facing scenario.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1/US2/US3/US4 — which spec.md user story this task belongs to
- Exact file paths are given in every description

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project. No new feature folder — every change lands inside the two already-existing folders
this unit bridges: `lib/features/chat/`, `lib/features/entries/`, plus `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` and
`lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. Tests mirror `lib/` under `test/`.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

**Purpose**: Confirm the starting state before extending it — no project-structure or dependency changes are
needed for this unit (plan.md: "No new feature folder... No additions" to `pubspec.yaml`).

- [ ] T001 Run `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` from the repo root to confirm a clean, green
  baseline before making any change in this unit.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The shared plumbing every user story depends on — the `BookmarkStatus` enum, the two new
visual tokens, the extended `CreateEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository` seam, and the device-local "already
saved" record on `ChatRepository`. None of this is itself a user-facing scenario; it is what Phase 3+ builds
on.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T002 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_status.dart` with
  `enum BookmarkStatus { idle, saving, saved, error }` — a bare enum (no `Equatable`, no `package:flutter`
  import, no `chat/data/` import), matching prototype-extract.md's four named sub-states one-to-one
  (data-model.md; RNF06/Principle V — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart`).

- [ ] T003 [P] Add two new constants to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`, alongside the existing
  `size*`/`spacing*` constants: `static const double sizeBookmarkIcon = 16;` and
  `static const double spacingBookmarkGap = 6;` — exact pixel values transcribed from
  `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html`'s own inline bookmark markup, not rounded to the existing 4dp
  grid (research.md R7, Principle IV).

- [ ] T004 Extend the abstract `EntriesRepository.create` in
  `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`: add two new optional named parameters,
  `String? chatMessageId` and `DateTime? occurredAt` (both default `null`), to the existing

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: Depends on Foundational. Delivers the MVP end-to-end.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: Depends on Foundational *and* on User Story 1's `_onBookmarkTapped`/
  `BookmarkButton` (T019/T021/T024) existing to verify against — it adds no new production code.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: Same — depends on Foundational and US1's T019/T021/T024, adds no new production
  code.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: Depends on Foundational and US1's T022/T023, adds no new production code.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Foundational: T004 gates T005/T006/T007 (all three extend callers of the interface T004 changes); T009/T010
  are independent of each other and of T002-T008, but T011 needs both.
- User Story 1: T014/T015 (event/state shapes) gate T016 (bloc wiring), which gates T017→T018→T019→T020. T021
  (widget) is independent of the bloc chain and only needs T002/T003; T022 needs T021; T023 needs T022 and
  T014. Tests T024-T026 need their respective implementation tasks done first.
- User Stories 2-4: each task lists its own single prerequisite from Foundational/US1 above; tasks within a
  phase are otherwise independent of each other.

### Parallel Opportunities

- All of T002, T003, T009, T010 (Foundational) can run in parallel — four different files, no shared
  dependency.
- T005, T006, T007 can run in parallel once T004 is done.
- T012 and T013 (chat-repository tests) can run in parallel once T011 is done.
- In User Story 1, T021 (the `BookmarkButton` widget) can be built in parallel with T014-T020 (the bloc/event/
  state chain) — they only converge at T022.
- Every `[P]`-marked test task within US2/US3/US4 can run in parallel with its siblings in the same phase.

```bash
Task: "Create BookmarkStatus enum in lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_status.dart"
Task: "Add sizeBookmarkIcon/spacingBookmarkGap to lib/core/design_tokens.dart"
```

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (blocks everything).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 — tap a message, get a persisted, restart-safe entry.
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: run quickstart.md Story 1 manually; this is already a demoable, shippable increment.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → shared plumbing ready.
2. User Story 1 → the MVP: save, persist, survive restart.
3. User Story 2 → verify the duplicate-prevention guarantee US1's own code already provides.
4. User Story 3 → verify failure isolation/retry US1's own code already provides.
5. User Story 4 → verify the user-only placement US1's own code already provides by construction.
6. Polish → coverage/lint/architecture gates, FR-010 scope check.

Unlike a typical feature where each story adds new code, US2-US4 here are deliberately verification-only
phases: the single `_onBookmarkTapped` handler and `ChatMessageBubble`/`BookmarkButton` composition built in
US1 already satisfy FR-004 (dedup), FR-005/FR-006/FR-007 (failure isolation), and FR-001 (user-only placement)
by construction (per spec.md's own Assumptions and research.md R6/R8/R9/R10) — so their phases schedule the
tests and manual checks that prove it, not new production code.

# Implementation Plan: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

**Branch**: `008-chat-message-bookmark` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-21 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/008-chat-message-bookmark/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF10), §6.2/6.3 (`entries-create`'s `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` fields, already documented as shared
between RF01 and RF10), §8 (data model reference — `entries.chat_message_id`), §12 (delivery order: RF10 after
RF01 and RF04, both already implemented), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` POST schema
(`chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` already accepted, optional, `format: uuid`/`format: date-time`);
`docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` ("Never `409` — the idempotency of RF10 ... always answers `200`");
`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.2 ("Tela 1 — Bookmark") and its inline component table; the
prototype's own source (`docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html`, the bookmark row's exact markup/styles);
and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF01 (`specs/003-multimodal-capture/`) and RF04
(`specs/007-chat-memory-rag/`), both already implemented — this is the unit that connects chat's own
messages to the entry-creation seam RF01 built and already annotated for this exact extension
(`create_entry_usecase.dart`: "RF10 will extend this signature, never bypass it").

## Summary

Every user message in Home/Chat gains a bookmark control with the prototype's own four sub-states — `idle`,
`saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning) — that turns that one message into a
persisted journal entry via the exact same `CreateEntryUseCase` RF01 already established, now extended with
two new optional parameters (`chatMessageId`, `occurredAt`) that thread straight through
`EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` to `entries-create`'s already-documented
request fields — no backend change, no new endpoint, no new repository. `ChatBloc` (RF04) gains exactly one
new dependency, `CreateEntryUseCase` itself (a domain usecase, never a repository or data source — the literal
seam FR-009 names), one new event (`BookmarkTapped(messageId)`), and one new `ChatReady` field (`bookmarks: Map<String,
BookmarkStatus>`, keyed by message id) tracking each message's bookmark sub-state in memory for the lifetime of
the bloc. `ChatRepository`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`/`ChatLocalCache` (also RF04) each gain a small, device-local,
Keychain-backed record of "which chat message ids have already produced an entry" (`savedEntryIdFor`/
`recordMessageSaved`) — a convenience for FR-008's "still shows `saved` after reopening/restarting," never the
source of correctness, since the backend's own `entries-create` idempotency (keyed by `chatMessageId`, confirmed
`200` not `409` on a repeat) already guarantees no duplicate regardless of what this local record remembers or
forgets. One new presentation widget, `BookmarkButton`, renders the four sub-states with two new, exact-value
`DesignTokens` (`sizeBookmarkIcon`, `spacingBookmarkGap`) read directly off the prototype's own inline bookmark
markup; `ChatMessageBubble`'s existing user-message branch is extended to lay the bubble and the bookmark
side by side in a row, matching that markup exactly. No change to `records/`, `export/`, `dashboard/`, any
backend file, or any file under `docs/input/`.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01–RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`,
`flutter_secure_storage` (for `ChatLocalCache`'s one new key), `dio` (via the already-registered
`entries-create` function, unchanged shape); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: One new key on the existing `ChatLocalCache` (`chatSavedMessageEntryIds` → `Map<String, String>`,
`chatMessageId` → `entryId`), same Keychain-backed, JSON-encoded mechanism `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`
already use for personal content (research.md R1). No new local-cache class, no new third-party persistence
package.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07) — now additionally exercising
`bookmark_status.dart` (a pure enum) and `ChatBloc`'s new `_onBookmarkTapped` branches (testable with the same
`MockChatRepository`/`MockCreateEntryUseCase`-via-`MockEntriesRepository` pattern `chat_bloc_test.dart`/
`create_entry_usecase_test.dart` already establish). `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` and
`domain_purity_test.dart` both run unmodified against the extended `lib/features/chat/` — no new bloc, no new
flutter/data import in `chat/domain/`. `test/architecture/no_cross_feature_data_imports_test.dart` (new,
already passing against the pre-RF10 codebase) is the one that enforces FR-009's actual constraint — no direct
`EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` import from `chat/presentation/bloc/` — which the other two tests
are not scoped to catch.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. No new feature folder — every change lands inside the two
already-existing folders this unit depends on (`lib/features/chat/`, `lib/features/entries/`), plus two
`core/` token additions and one `core/di/` registration update. No backend/server code, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (its `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` fields on `entries-create` already
exist and are simply used for the first time).

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The bookmark's `saving` state (shown the instant the tap is handled,
before the network call resolves) is this unit's own "<100 ms local reflection"; the spinner itself is the
required loading indicator for the network call that follows (always well past the 300 ms threshold in
practice for a write endpoint already doing PII-check + embedding server-side).

**Constraints**:
- No RF08 (proactive insight)/RF05 (export)/RF09 (dashboard), no extension feature, no backend/contract/
  config change (FR-010) — `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` are fields `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`
  already declares on `entries-create`'s request body; nothing new is sent that the contract doesn't already
  define.
- Entry creation from chat MUST go through `CreateEntryUseCase` only, never `EntriesRepository`/
  `EntriesRemoteDataSource` directly (FR-009) — enforced by construction: `chat_bloc.dart`'s only new import
  from `features/entries/` is `create_entry_usecase.dart` (+ `entry.dart` for the `EntrySource` enum already
  used identically by every other `source` value chat never touches otherwise).
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — the one new domain file,
  `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_status.dart`, is a bare enum: no `package:flutter`, no
  `chat/data/` import (confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart`, unmodified). `ChatBloc`'s dependency
  surface grows by exactly one domain usecase (`CreateEntryUseCase`) — no new cross-bloc import.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every bookmark
  color is reused verbatim (`colorTextSecondary`/`colorAccent`/`colorError`, already defined); the icon size
  (16 dp) and the bubble-to-icon gap (6 dp) are new, exact-value tokens (`sizeBookmarkIcon`,
  `spacingBookmarkGap`) because neither matches an existing 4 dp-grid step, mirroring the precedent already set
  by `sizeAudioRecordIcon`/`sizePhotoTileIcon`/`borderWidthFocused` (RF01–RF03) for off-grid, element-specific
  values read straight off the prototype.
- Idempotency (FR-004) is **not** reimplemented client-side — it is the backend's own guarantee
  (`error-taxonomy.md`: "Never `409`... always answers `200`"). The device-local `savedEntryIdFor` record is
  explicitly a convenience for FR-008's UI-continuity requirement, never a correctness mechanism (spec.md's own
  Assumptions already say so) — this plan does not invent a second, client-side dedup guarantee on top of it.

**Scale/Scope**: 0 new feature folders. 1 new domain entity (`bookmark_status.dart`), 1 new presentation widget
(`bookmark_button.dart`); 8 existing files extended (`create_entry_usecase.dart`, `entries_repository.dart`,
`entries_repository_impl.dart`, `entries_remote_data_source.dart`, `chat_repository.dart`,
`chat_repository_impl.dart`, `chat_local_cache.dart`, `chat_event.dart`/`chat_state.dart`/`chat_bloc.dart`,
`chat_message_bubble.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`); 2 new `DesignTokens` constants; 1 DI registration
updated (no new registration — `CreateEntryUseCase` is already registered by RF01).

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only throughout. Every judgment call below (research.md R1–R10) fills a gap spec.md itself already flags as "an implementation decision for the planning phase" (FR-009's shared-interface shape, FR-003's `saved`-state non-tappability) or that neither `requirements.md` nor the prototype addresses (the optimistic-message-id race, R6; the device-local record's exact storage shape, R1) — none reopens a Clarification spec.md already resolved. |
| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No new package. `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/`flutter_secure_storage` all already project dependencies. |
| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only the already-contracted `entries-create` function is called, now with two of its already-declared optional request fields (`chatMessageId`/`occurredAt`) populated for the first time; no AI provider called directly; no OpenAPI/`.env`/config file touched. |
| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | Every bookmark color reused verbatim; the two new size/spacing tokens are exact values transcribed from the prototype's own inline bookmark markup (research.md R7), not approximations. |
| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `bookmark_status.dart` imports nothing beyond the Dart core library; `ChatBloc`'s new dependency (`CreateEntryUseCase`) is a domain usecase, not a repository/data source — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart`/`no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` (unmodified) and the new, narrowly-scoped `test/architecture/no_cross_feature_data_imports_test.dart`, which is the one that actually catches `chat_bloc.dart` importing `EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` directly. |
| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | The `saving` state is this unit's own instant local reflection; the spinner is the loading indicator the network call (always realistically >300 ms for a PII-check+embedding write) requires. |
| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to RF10 directly | Chat-sourced entries run through the exact same backend `entries-create` pipeline as every other source (spec.md Assumptions) — no new client-side PII logic, no new retention policy, RLS unaffected (same `auth.uid() = user_id` entries table). |
| RNF05 (hard delete) | N/A | Belongs to Settings/RNF05's own unit. |
| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | `chat/domain/` stays flutter/data-free; `ChatBloc` never imports `EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` (FR-009's own wording is also RNF06's own concern per spec.md: "a violation here also breaks RNF06") — confirmed by `chat_bloc.dart`'s planned import list containing only `create_entry_usecase.dart`/`entry.dart` from `features/entries/`. |
| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | `bookmark_status.dart` is a trivial enum (same tier as `EntrySource`/`ChatRole`); the more substantial new logic (`_seedBookmarks`, `_onBookmarkTapped`'s branches, `ChatRepositoryImpl.savedEntryIdFor`/`recordMessageSaved`) is tested the same `mocktail`-driven way every other `ChatBloc`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` branch already is. |
| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | Bookmark icon/size/color/gap/spin-animation match the prototype's own inline bookmark markup exactly (research.md R7) — transcribed, not approximated. |
| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | No new write endpoint — `entries-create` is already one of RNF09's counted 5 endpoints (its 3 base failure scenarios already covered by RF01's own tests); this unit adds scenario-table rows specific to the bookmark path (idempotent-retry outcome, `AuthExpiredFailure` → `reauthRequired`) on top of, not instead of, that existing coverage (contracts/create-entry-usecase-chat-extension.md). |

*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/008-chat-message-bookmark/
├── plan.md                                          # This file
├── research.md                                      # Phase 0 output
├── data-model.md                                    # Phase 1 output

│   ├── create-entry-usecase-chat-extension.md
│   ├── chat-repository-bookmark-extension.md

```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
cerne-ciclo-a/
└── lib/
    ├── core/
    │   ├── design_tokens.dart                         # + sizeBookmarkIcon, spacingBookmarkGap (research.md R7)
    │   └── di/
    │       └── service_locator.dart                   # ChatBloc registration + createEntryUseCase param
    └── features/
        ├── entries/
        │   ├── domain/
        │   │   ├── usecases/
        │   │   │   └── create_entry_usecase.dart       # + chatMessageId/occurredAt params (research.md R2)
        │   │   └── repositories/
        │   │       └── entries_repository.dart         # create() signature extended, same params
        │   └── data/
        │       ├── entries_repository_impl.dart        # create() passes the two new params through
        │       └── entries_remote_data_source.dart      # create() sends them in the request body when non-null
        └── chat/
            ├── domain/
            │   ├── entities/
            │   │   └── bookmark_status.dart             # NEW — enum { idle, saving, saved, error }
            │   └── repositories/
            │       └── chat_repository.dart              # + savedEntryIdFor / recordMessageSaved (research.md R1)
            ├── data/
            │   ├── chat_local_cache.dart                 # + chatSavedMessageEntryIds key/methods
            │   └── chat_repository_impl.dart              # + the two new methods, 1 new in-memory field
            └── presentation/
                ├── bloc/
                │   ├── chat_event.dart                    # + BookmarkTapped(messageId)
                │   ├── chat_state.dart                    # + ChatReady.bookmarks, bookmarkStatusFor()
                │   └── chat_bloc.dart                      # + CreateEntryUseCase dep, _onBookmarkTapped, _seedBookmarks
                └── widgets/
                    ├── bookmark_button.dart                # NEW — 4-state icon control
                    └── chat_message_bubble.dart             # extended — bubble+bookmark row for user messages
        └── home/
            └── presentation/
```

**Structure Decision**: No new feature folder. Every change lands inside `chat/` and `entries/`, the two
folders FR-009 itself names as the ones this unit bridges — `chat/` gains the one new domain enum a bookmark

extension point (`CreateEntryUseCase`'s own doc comment has said "RF10 will extend this signature" since RF01
shipped). `core/design_tokens.dart` and `core/di/service_locator.dart` are touched because they are the two
single-source-of-truth files every unit touches when it needs a new visual value or a new DI wire-up — not
because this unit needs its own `core/` subsystem the way RF04's SSE transport did.

## Complexity Tracking

> **Fill ONLY if Constitution Check has violations that must be justified** — no row below is a violation;
> each documents a design choice research.md reasons through in full, kept here for traceability only.

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| A device-local `savedEntryIdFor`/`recordMessageSaved` pair on `ChatRepository`, instead of deriving "already saved" from `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` | FR-008 needs a message's bookmark to show `saved` immediately on reopening a conversation/restarting the app; `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` is a synchronous getter with its own independent, unrelated lazy-load timing (research.md R1) not guaranteed populated by the time `ChatBloc` loads a session | Reading `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` directly from `ChatBloc` — rejected: couples a chat-local UI concern to a different feature's cache-loading lifecycle, and (per FR-009's own spirit, even though `cachedEntries` is a repository getter, not a creation path) adds a needless second entries-feature dependency to `ChatBloc` for a question `chat/`'s own local cache can already answer on its own |
| No dedicated `SaveChatMessageUseCase` wrapping `CreateEntryUseCase` + `ChatRepository.recordMessageSaved` | `ChatBloc` already has direct, synchronous access to the tapped message's `content`/`createdAt`/`id` — the two calls the bloc's own handler makes have no behavior of their own beyond what `_onBookmarkTapped` already needs inline (research.md R4, the same judgment RF04's own research.md R13 already made for every other `ChatBloc` handler) | A wrapper use case — rejected: zero added testability over mocking `CreateEntryUseCase`/`ChatRepository` directly at the same level `chat_bloc_test.dart` already mocks `ChatRepository`, for one extra file and DI registration |
| Guarding `_onBookmarkTapped` against an optimistic (`isOptimistic == true`) message id as a silent no-op | A message can render its bookmark before the backend assigns its real id (between the optimistic append and `message_created`); sending a `local-<timestamp>` string as `chatMessageId` would violate the OpenAPI field's `format: uuid` and either get rejected or write bad data — neither spec.md nor the prototype (which has no server-roundtrip concept) addresses this race (research.md R6) | Disabling/hiding the bookmark entirely while a message is optimistic — rejected: FR-001 requires the control to appear on every user message with no exceptions; a silent no-op tap, exactly like the already-established "ignore a tap while `saving`" pattern (FR-007), satisfies both FR-001 (always visible) and correctness (never sends a malformed id) without a new visual state |

## Post-Design Constitution Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):

- `bookmark_status.dart`'s planned import list re-checked: empty beyond Dart core — no `equatable` even needed
  for a plain enum, no `package:flutter`, no `chat/data/` class. RNF06/Principle V confirmed before any code
  exists.
- `ChatBloc`'s planned constructor re-checked: `ChatRepository` + `ConnectivityChecker` (unchanged) +
  `CreateEntryUseCase` (new) — no `EntriesRepository`, no `EntriesRemoteDataSource`, no second bloc. FR-009's
  "never directly import a repository or data source belonging to the entries feature" holds by construction
  and is now also mechanically checked by `test/architecture/no_cross_feature_data_imports_test.dart` (T042).
- Re-checked `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create()`'s extended request-body construction against the OpenAPI
  schema: `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` are both already-declared, optional, correctly-typed fields — nothing
  sent that the contract doesn't already define (Principle III).
- Re-checked that every existing caller of `CreateEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository.create`/
  `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create` (`SaveTextEntryUseCase`, `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`, and their manual/audio/
  photo call sites) omits both new named parameters and is therefore byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged — no
  regression risk to RF01/RF02.
- Re-checked the two new `DesignTokens` constants against the prototype's own inline bookmark styles
  (16 px icon, 6 px gap) — exact transcription, confirmed in research.md R7.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file,
  or calls an AI provider directly — Principle III remains intact.

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

166	  final String messageId;

217	Map<String, BookmarkStatus> _seedBookmarks(List<ChatMessage> messages) {
218	  final result = <String, BookmarkStatus>{};
219	  for (final m in messages) {
220	    if (m.role != ChatRole.user) continue;
221	    if (_chatRepository.savedEntryIdFor(m.id) != null) result[m.id] = BookmarkStatus.saved;
222	  }
223	  return result;

226	Future<void> _onBookmarkTapped(BookmarkTapped event, Emitter<ChatState> emit) async {
227	  final current = state;
228	  if (current is! ChatReady) return;
229	  final index = current.messages.indexWhere((m) => m.id == event.messageId);
230	  if (index == -1) return;
231	  final message = current.messages[index];
232	  if (message.role != ChatRole.user || message.isOptimistic) return;   // research.md R6
233	  final status = current.bookmarkStatusFor(message.id);
234	  if (status == BookmarkStatus.saving || status == BookmarkStatus.saved) return;   // FR-003/FR-007
235	
236	  emit(current.copyWith(bookmarks: {...current.bookmarks, message.id: BookmarkStatus.saving}));
237	
238	  final created = await _createEntryUseCase(
239	    message.content,
240	    EntrySource.chat,
241	    chatMessageId: message.id,
242	    occurredAt: message.createdAt,
243	  );
244	
245	  final latest = state;
246	  if (latest is! ChatReady) return;
247	
248	  await created.match(
249	    (failure) async {
250	      if (failure is AuthExpiredFailure) _reauthController.add(null);   // research.md R9
251	      emit(latest.copyWith(bookmarks: {...latest.bookmarks, message.id: BookmarkStatus.error}));
252	    },
253	    (entry) async {
254	      await _chatRepository.recordMessageSaved(chatMessageId: message.id, entryId: entry.id);
255	      final afterRecord = state;
256	      if (afterRecord is! ChatReady) return;
257	      emit(afterRecord.copyWith(bookmarks: {...afterRecord.bookmarks, message.id: BookmarkStatus.saved}));
258	    },
259	  );
260	}

2	
3	Extends the interface `specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/entries-repository.md` and
4	`specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/save-usecases.md` already define — `create`'s existing two required
5	parameters (`content`, `source`) are unchanged; this unit only adds two optional named ones, exactly the
6	extension `create_entry_usecase.dart`'s own doc comment has named since RF01 shipped.
7	
8	```dart
9	class CreateEntryUseCase {
10	  const CreateEntryUseCase(this._repository);
11	  final EntriesRepository _repository;
12	
13	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> call(
14	    String content,
15	    EntrySource source, {
16	    String? chatMessageId,
17	    DateTime? occurredAt,
18	  }) => _repository.create(
19	    content: content,
20	    source: source,
21	    chatMessageId: chatMessageId,
22	    occurredAt: occurredAt,
23	  );
24	}

26	
27	```dart
28	abstract class EntriesRepository {
29	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
30	    required String content,
31	    required EntrySource source,
32	    String? chatMessageId,
33	    DateTime? occurredAt,
34	  });
35	  // list / getById / search / cachedEntries — unchanged, see 003/005/006's own contracts
36	}
37	```
38	
39	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` (orchestration, data layer) — unchanged shape, 2 new pass-through params
40	
41	```dart
42	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
43	  required String content,
44	  required EntrySource source,
45	  String? chatMessageId,
46	  DateTime? occurredAt,
47	}) async {
48	  await _ensureLocalCacheLoaded();
49	  final result = await _remoteDataSource.create(
50	    content: content,
51	    source: source,
52	    chatMessageId: chatMessageId,
53	    occurredAt: occurredAt,
54	  );
55	  return result.match(
56	    (failure) => Future.value(Left(failure)),
57	    (entry) async {
58	      await _cacheAndPersist([entry]);
59	      return Right(entry);
60	    },
61	  );
62	}
63	```
64	
65	No retry-on-`AuthExpiredFailure` is added here (research.md R9) — `create()` has never had one (RF01), and
66	this unit doesn't add it; `ChatBloc`'s own `_onBookmarkTapped` fires `reauthRequired` on that specific failure
67	instead (contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md).

71	```dart
72	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
73	  required String content,
74	  required EntrySource source,
75	  String? chatMessageId,
76	  DateTime? occurredAt,
77	}) async {
78	  final result = await _apiClient.call(
79	    'entries-create',
80	    method: 'POST',
81	    body: {
82	      'content': content,
83	      'source': source.name,
84	      if (chatMessageId != null) 'chatMessageId': chatMessageId,
85	      if (occurredAt != null) 'occurredAt': occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),

94	sent by any caller in this app.

99	new parameters. Every existing caller — `SaveTextEntryUseCase`, `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase` (RF01/RF02) — omits

103	
104	| # | Scenario | Expected |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| 1 | `create(content, EntrySource.manual)` — no new params | Request body unchanged (no `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` keys) — confirms zero regression for every existing caller |
107	| 2 | `create(content, EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: 'uuid-1', occurredAt: t)` | Request body includes both: `{'chatMessageId': 'uuid-1', 'occurredAt': t.toUtc().toIso8601String()}` alongside `content`/`source` |

1	# Research: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
2	
3	Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where these
4	documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
5	clarification"). None reopens spec.md's own already-resolved calls (FR-003's `saved`-state non-tappability,
6	FR-009's "shared interface" requirement) — each item below fills in a mechanical detail those, the OpenAPI
7	contract, or the prototype extract leave open.
8	
9	## R1 — Where does "this message was already saved" live for FR-008's restart-safety?
10	
11	**Decision**: `ChatRepository` (domain) gains two new members:
12	
13	```dart
14	String? savedEntryIdFor(String chatMessageId);
15	Future<void> recordMessageSaved({required String chatMessageId, required String entryId});
16	```
17	
18	`savedEntryIdFor` is a synchronous read of an in-memory `Map<String, String>` that `ChatRepositoryImpl` loads
19	from a new `ChatLocalCache` key (`chatSavedMessageEntryIds`) inside the exact same `_ensureLocalCacheLoaded()`
20	future every other `ChatRepositoryImpl` method already awaits before returning
21	(`createSession`/`listSessions`/`listMessages` all await it today). `ChatBloc` only ever calls
22	`savedEntryIdFor` from inside `_loadSession`, strictly after `listMessages(sessionId)` has resolved — which
23	means `_ensureLocalCacheLoaded()` has, by construction, already completed, so the read is always safe without
24	needing its own `await`. `recordMessageSaved` upserts the map and persists it via a new
25	`ChatLocalCache.writeSavedMessageEntryIds()`, called once, right after a bookmark's `CreateEntryUseCase` call
26	succeeds.
27	
28	**Rationale**: this is a device-local, per-viewer convenience exactly as spec.md's own Assumptions describe it
29	("a device-local record of which messages this client has already saved; that record is a convenience, not a
30	correctness mechanism") — mirroring the identical shape `ChatLocalCache` already uses for
31	`chatSessionsLocalCache`/`chatMessagesLocalCache`/`chatLastActiveSessionId` (three independent keys, one
32	lazy-loaded future, each read only after that future is known to have resolved). Keeping it behind
33	`ChatRepository` (never exposed as a raw `ChatLocalCache` read to `ChatBloc`) preserves the same
34	presentation-depends-on-repository-only layering every other bloc in this codebase already observes.
35	
36	**Alternatives considered**: deriving "already saved" by scanning `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` for a
37	`chatMessageId` match — rejected (see plan.md's Complexity Tracking): `cachedEntries` is a synchronous getter
38	over a *different* feature's own independently-lazy-loaded cache, with no guarantee it has been populated by
39	the time `ChatBloc` loads a session (nothing in this unit's flow calls any `EntriesRepository` method before
40	that point), and reading it would add a needless second `entries/`-feature dependency to `ChatBloc` for a
41	question `chat/`'s own local cache can answer by itself. A brand-new, separate `BookmarkLocalCache` class —
42	rejected: `ChatLocalCache` already exists, already mirrors `EntriesLocalCache`'s exact per-feature-cache
43	rationale, and a 4th independent key costs nothing a new class would also need (same constructor, same
44	`FlutterSecureStorage` instance, same JSON-encode-on-write pattern).
45	
46	## R2 — Extending `CreateEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository.create` without touching existing callers
47	
48	**Decision**: add two optional, named parameters — `chatMessageId` and `occurredAt`, both defaulting to
49	`null` — through all four layers already in the create path: `CreateEntryUseCase.call`,
50	`EntriesRepository.create`, `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create`, `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create`.
51	`EntriesRemoteDataSource.create`'s request body includes `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` only when each is
52	non-null (the same optional-field-omission style `list`/`search` already use for their own optional query
53	parameters), exactly matching the OpenAPI schema (`entries-create`'s request body: `chatMessageId` —
54	`format: uuid`, optional; `occurredAt` — `format: date-time`, optional).
55	
56	**Rationale**: `create_entry_usecase.dart`'s own doc comment has named this extension point since RF01 shipped
57	("RF10 will extend this signature, never bypass it"). Positional-with-named-optional-additions is the only
58	shape that leaves every existing call site (`SaveTextEntryUseCase`'s and `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`'s three
59	manual/audio/photo sites) byte-for-byte untouched — they already call `_createEntryUseCase(content, source)`
60	positionally, which remains valid with the new named parameters simply omitted.
61	
62	**Alternatives considered**: a parallel `CreateChatEntryUseCase` class — rejected, FR-009 explicitly wants
63	*one* shared interface every feature creating an entry depends on, not a second, chat-specific one that would
64	duplicate `CreateEntryUseCase`'s single orchestration line for no behavioral difference; making the two new
65	fields positional — rejected, would force every existing call site to be edited for no reason.
66	
67	## R3 — `occurredAt`'s value
68	
69	**Decision**: the bookmark flow always passes the originating `ChatMessage.createdAt` (the message's own send
70	time) as `occurredAt`, exactly as spec.md's Assumptions state ("the chat message's own `createdAt` timestamp...
71	not the moment the user taps the bookmark"). Every other existing caller continues to omit `occurredAt`
72	entirely, leaving the backend's own default (creation time = now) exactly as it behaves today for manual/
73	audio/photo entries — confirmed no regression, since the parameter is optional and no current caller passes
74	it.
75	
76	**Rationale**: a bookmark can be tapped well after the message was sent (the user keeps chatting, then later
77	taps an earlier message's bookmark) — using "now" instead of the message's own `createdAt` would place the
78	resulting entry at the wrong point in the user's timeline, the exact failure mode the Assumption calls out.
79	
80	## R4 — Where the bookmark's orchestration logic lives
81	
82	**Decision**: `ChatBloc` gains exactly one new constructor dependency, `CreateEntryUseCase` — the sanctioned
83	shared seam FR-009 names directly, never `EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` — and handles the whole
84	bookmark flow inline via one new event (`BookmarkTapped(messageId)`) and one new private handler
85	(`_onBookmarkTapped`). No dedicated `SaveChatMessageUseCase`/`BookmarkRepository` class is introduced.
86	
87	**Rationale**: this is the identical judgment RF04's own research.md R13 already made for every other
88	`ChatBloc` handler ("no extra use-case layer... every event it handles belongs to the one conversation
89	screen's one flow"). The bookmark handler needs exactly two calls — `CreateEntryUseCase(...)` and, on success,
90	`ChatRepository.recordMessageSaved(...)` — neither of which has any behavior of its own beyond what the
91	handler already needs inline (resolve the message by id, guard its current status, emit `saving`, await the
92	result, emit `saved`/`error`). A separate `BookmarkBloc` was also considered and rejected: it would either need
93	to duplicate `ChatBloc`'s own `messages` list (to resolve a `messageId` to its `content`/`createdAt`) or import
94	`ChatBloc` directly, which this codebase's established "no BLoC imports another BLoC directly" convention
95	(RF07's own acceptance criterion, reinforced by RF04's research.md R7) forbids.
96	
97	**Alternatives considered**: a `SaveChatMessageUseCase` wrapping both calls for symmetry with `capture/`'s
98	use-case classes — rejected, `capture/`'s use cases exist because `InsertionModalBloc` fans out across several
99	structurally different tabs each needing an independently-testable "what does Save do here" unit; `ChatBloc`'s
100	bookmark flow has no such fan-out, so the wrapper would add a file and a DI registration with zero
101	testability gain over mocking `CreateEntryUseCase`/`ChatRepository` directly, the same level every other
102	`ChatBloc` test already mocks at.
103	
104	## R5 — Per-message bookmark state representation
105	
106	**Decision**: `ChatReady` gains one new field, `Map<String, BookmarkStatus> bookmarks` (default `const {}`,
107	keyed by `ChatMessage.id`; an absent key means `idle`), plus a helper
108	`BookmarkStatus bookmarkStatusFor(String messageId) => bookmarks[messageId] ?? BookmarkStatus.idle`.
109	`BookmarkStatus` is a new, plain 4-value enum (`idle`, `saving`, `saved`, `error`) in
110	`lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_status.dart`, matching prototype-extract.md's own four named
111	sub-states one-to-one — `ChatMessageBubble`/`BookmarkButton` render directly off it with no translation layer.
112	Whenever `_loadSession` (re)loads a conversation's messages — on `ChatStarted` or `ConversationSelected`, both
113	the cache-fallback and the online-success branch — a new private helper, `_seedBookmarks(messages)`, rebuilds
114	the `bookmarks` map from scratch: for every `role == user` message, it calls
115	`_chatRepository.savedEntryIdFor(m.id)`; a non-null result seeds that message's entry as `saved`, otherwise it
116	is left absent (i.e. `idle`). This is the whole mechanism behind FR-008 — no separate "restore bookmarks" step,
117	no polling.
118	
119	**Rationale**: spec.md's own Key Entities section is explicit that "Bookmark" is "per-message, per-viewer UI
120	state... [that] never itself becomes a persisted record" — a plain side-table keyed by message id, parallel to
121	(not merged into) `messages`, matches that description directly. Folding a `bookmarkStatus` field onto
122	`ChatMessage` itself was the other option and was rejected: `ChatMessage` already matches `chat-messages-list`'s
123	response schema field-for-field (data-model.md's own stated precedent from RF04) and the backend schema has no
124	such field; adding one would blur a transport-shaped entity with a client-only UI concern, and would force
125	every one of `ChatBloc`'s existing `_withId`/`_withContent`/`_withStatus` copy-helpers to additionally thread a
126	field they have no reason to touch today.
127	
128	**Alternatives considered**: as above (field on `ChatMessage`) — rejected for the reasons given; computing
129	`bookmarkStatusFor` by scanning `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` every time it's called, instead of seeding a
130	map once at load time — rejected as both slower (an O(n) scan per message per rebuild) and reintroducing the
131	exact cross-feature-cache-timing coupling R1 already rejected.
132	
133	## R6 — Guarding the one race the prototype's own simulation doesn't model: an optimistic message id
134	
135	**Decision**: `_onBookmarkTapped` resolves the target message by id and, before doing anything else, returns
136	(a silent no-op) if that message's `isOptimistic` getter is `true` (the existing `id.startsWith('local-')`
137	check `ChatMessage` already defines) — i.e., the backend has not yet assigned this message its real id via
138	`message_created`. The bookmark remains visible and visually `idle`/tappable; the tap is simply swallowed, the
139	same way a tap on an already-`saving` bookmark is (FR-007's own "ignored" language).
140	
141	**Rationale**: a user message is appended to `ChatReady.messages` the instant it's typed (RNF01's optimistic
142	placeholder, RF04's research.md R5), with a client-generated `'local-<timestamp>'` id, before the backend's
143	`message_created` SSE event assigns the real one. The bookmark control is rendered for every user message
144	regardless of status (FR-001 has no exception for "message not yet acknowledged by the server"), so a tap
145	during that narrow window is reachable in principle. Sending a `'local-...'` string as `chatMessageId` would
146	violate the OpenAPI field's own `format: uuid` constraint and either get rejected outright or (worse) write an
147	entry with a `chatMessageId` that resolves to nothing once reconciliation happens. Neither `requirements.md`
148	nor the prototype (whose own simulated bookmark has no server-roundtrip concept at all — every message id is
149	assigned client-side, synchronously, forever) describes this race, so Principle I's "reasonable technical
150	decision" applies directly.
151	
152	**Alternatives considered**: hiding/disabling the bookmark visually while a message is optimistic — rejected,
153	FR-001 requires the control present on every user message "with no exceptions," and a new, narrower
154	disabled-look state is unneeded complexity when a silent no-op (identical in spirit to the already-specified
155	"ignore a tap while `saving`" behavior) is simpler and satisfies both FR-001 and correctness at once; queuing
156	the tap to fire automatically once the real id arrives — rejected as speculative scope nothing in spec.md asks
157	for, for a window typically sub-second long in practice.
158	
159	## R7 — Icon/token mapping (visual fidelity, RNF08)
160	
161	**Decision**: transcribed directly from the prototype's own inline bookmark markup
162	(`docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html`): a 16 dp icon, bottom-aligned in the same row as the user bubble
163	(not inside it), with a 6 dp gap between bubble and icon; colors `#6B6255` (`DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary`,
164	`idle`/`saving`), `#C98A3E` (`DesignTokens.colorAccent`, `saved`), `#B3402A` (`DesignTokens.colorError`,
165	`error`); a continuous 1 s linear spin only in `saving`. Two new `DesignTokens` constants are added for the two
166	values with no existing match on the 4 dp spacing/size scale — `sizeBookmarkIcon = 16` and
167	`spacingBookmarkGap = 6` — following the exact precedent `sizeAudioRecordIcon`/`sizePhotoTileIcon`/
168	`borderWidthFocused` (RF01–RF03) already set for off-grid, element-specific values read straight off the
169	prototype rather than rounded to the nearest 4 dp step. Every color is reused verbatim — zero new color
170	tokens.
171	
172	Icon glyphs: this codebase has no Phosphor dependency (every prior unit already substitutes a
173	semantically-equivalent Material glyph — e.g. `capture_status_views.dart` already maps the prototype's
174	`warning-circle` to `Icons.error_outline`). Mapping used here: `idle` → `Icons.bookmark_border`; `saving` → the
175	same rotating-arc technique `CaptureLoadingIndicator` already establishes (`RotationTransition` over a
176	fixed-sweep `CircularProgressIndicator`), reused at the new 16 dp size; `saved` → `Icons.check` (the
177	prototype's own choice is a plain checkmark, `ph-check`, not a circled one); `error` → `Icons.error_outline`
178	(the exact glyph/color pairing `RecognitionErrorView` already uses for the same "red warning" semantic).
179	
180	**Rationale**: Principle IV requires every visual value to trace to the prototype through `design_tokens.dart`
181	with zero hardcoding elsewhere; reading the actual rendered pixel values out of the prototype's own source
182	(rather than approximating with the nearest existing 4 dp token) is the only way to satisfy RNF08's "spacing
183	matches the prototype" for a value that genuinely isn't a multiple of 4.
184	
185	**Alternatives considered**: rounding 6 dp up to the existing `spacingSm` (8 dp) to avoid adding a token —
186	rejected, a visible, measurable deviation from the prototype for no reason stronger than "avoid one constant";
187	adding the `phosphor_flutter` package to render the prototype's exact glyphs — rejected, new dependency for
188	icons every prior unit already substitutes with Material equivalents without it.
189	
190	## R8 — Widget composition and placement
191	
192	**Decision**: a new, small `BookmarkButton` widget (`lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/bookmark_button.dart`),
193	taking `(BookmarkStatus status, VoidCallback? onTap)`. Its own `GestureDetector` is **omitted entirely** (not
194	merely disabled) whenever `status` is `saving` or `saved` — matching FR-003's literal wording ("carries no tap
195	handler") rather than only its visual appearance. `ChatMessageBubble`'s existing `_isUser` branch is extended:
196	the bubble `Container` and a `BookmarkButton` are wrapped in a `Row` (`crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end`,
197	a `spacingBookmarkGap`-wide gap between them), replacing the bare bubble, matching the prototype's own
198	row-wrapped markup (bubble + bookmark bottom-aligned, gap 6 dp, timestamp below the whole row — unchanged).
199	The assistant branch is untouched; `BookmarkButton` is never instantiated there, so FR-001's "no exceptions" —
200	including insight cards and streaming/failed assistant bubbles, none of which are rendered by the `_isUser`
201	branch at all — holds by construction, not by an extra conditional.
202	
203	**Rationale**: matches the prototype's own markup structure exactly (a `flex` row containing the bubble and
204	the bookmark icon, bottom-aligned, the timestamp below) rather than approximating a different layout.
205	Omitting the `GestureDetector`/tap region entirely for `saving`/`saved` (rather than wrapping it and setting
206	`onTap: null`, which Flutter's own `GestureDetector` already treats as inert, but would still carry a widget
207	whose *name* suggests interactivity) keeps the implementation legible against FR-003's specific wording.
208	
209	**Alternatives considered**: a single `AnimatedSwitcher`-driven icon swap with an always-present
210	`GestureDetector` guarded only by a `null` callback — rejected as functionally equivalent but less literal
211	against FR-003's "carries no tap handler," and not meaningfully simpler to write.
212	
213	## R9 — Session-expiry handling during a bookmark save (Edge Cases)
214	
215	**Decision**: `_onBookmarkTapped`'s failure branch checks `if (failure is AuthExpiredFailure)
216	_reauthController.add(null);` before setting the bookmark to `error` — the exact same one-line pattern
217	`_consumeTurn`'s `_applyFailure` branch and `_loadSession`'s failure branch already use for every other
218	`AuthExpiredFailure` this bloc can see. The bookmark itself still ends in `error` (retryable) either way; no
219	silent-refresh-and-retry is added to `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` itself.
220	
221	**Rationale**: spec.md's Edge Cases explicitly names this path ("the existing overlay takes over as it already
222	does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the bookmark reflects the save's actual outcome rather
223	than being stuck mid-attempt"). Firing `reauthRequired` raises the same "Sessão expirada" overlay every other
224	auth-expiry path in this screen already raises; leaving the bookmark in `error` (rather than inventing an
225	auto-retry) satisfies "reflects the save's actual outcome" (a failed attempt did, in fact, fail) while staying
226	tappable once the user re-authenticates and taps again — no new state, no new retry machinery.
227

235

240	
241	**Rationale**: spec.md's own Acceptance Scenario (US3 Scenario 1) describes tapping while offline as
242	transitioning through `saving` and landing on `error` ("the control shows a saving indicator... and, instead

# Research: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where these
documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
clarification"). None reopens spec.md's own already-resolved calls (FR-003's `saved`-state non-tappability,
FR-009's "shared interface" requirement) — each item below fills in a mechanical detail those, the OpenAPI
contract, or the prototype extract leave open.

## R1 — Where does "this message was already saved" live for FR-008's restart-safety?

**Decision**: `ChatRepository` (domain) gains two new members:

```dart
String? savedEntryIdFor(String chatMessageId);
Future<void> recordMessageSaved({required String chatMessageId, required String entryId});
```

`savedEntryIdFor` is a synchronous read of an in-memory `Map<String, String>` that `ChatRepositoryImpl` loads
from a new `ChatLocalCache` key (`chatSavedMessageEntryIds`) inside the exact same `_ensureLocalCacheLoaded()`
future every other `ChatRepositoryImpl` method already awaits before returning
(`createSession`/`listSessions`/`listMessages` all await it today). `ChatBloc` only ever calls
`savedEntryIdFor` from inside `_loadSession`, strictly after `listMessages(sessionId)` has resolved — which
means `_ensureLocalCacheLoaded()` has, by construction, already completed, so the read is always safe without
needing its own `await`. `recordMessageSaved` upserts the map and persists it via a new
`ChatLocalCache.writeSavedMessageEntryIds()`, called once, right after a bookmark's `CreateEntryUseCase` call
succeeds.

**Rationale**: this is a device-local, per-viewer convenience exactly as spec.md's own Assumptions describe it
("a device-local record of which messages this client has already saved; that record is a convenience, not a
correctness mechanism") — mirroring the identical shape `ChatLocalCache` already uses for
`chatSessionsLocalCache`/`chatMessagesLocalCache`/`chatLastActiveSessionId` (three independent keys, one
lazy-loaded future, each read only after that future is known to have resolved). Keeping it behind
`ChatRepository` (never exposed as a raw `ChatLocalCache` read to `ChatBloc`) preserves the same
presentation-depends-on-repository-only layering every other bloc in this codebase already observes.

**Alternatives considered**: deriving "already saved" by scanning `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` for a
`chatMessageId` match — rejected (see plan.md's Complexity Tracking): `cachedEntries` is a synchronous getter
over a *different* feature's own independently-lazy-loaded cache, with no guarantee it has been populated by
the time `ChatBloc` loads a session (nothing in this unit's flow calls any `EntriesRepository` method before
that point), and reading it would add a needless second `entries/`-feature dependency to `ChatBloc` for a
question `chat/`'s own local cache can answer by itself. A brand-new, separate `BookmarkLocalCache` class —
rejected: `ChatLocalCache` already exists, already mirrors `EntriesLocalCache`'s exact per-feature-cache
rationale, and a 4th independent key costs nothing a new class would also need (same constructor, same
`FlutterSecureStorage` instance, same JSON-encode-on-write pattern).

## R2 — Extending `CreateEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository.create` without touching existing callers

**Decision**: add two optional, named parameters — `chatMessageId` and `occurredAt`, both defaulting to
`null` — through all four layers already in the create path: `CreateEntryUseCase.call`,
`EntriesRepository.create`, `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create`, `EntriesRemoteDataSource.create`.
`EntriesRemoteDataSource.create`'s request body includes `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt` only when each is
non-null (the same optional-field-omission style `list`/`search` already use for their own optional query
parameters), exactly matching the OpenAPI schema (`entries-create`'s request body: `chatMessageId` —
`format: uuid`, optional; `occurredAt` — `format: date-time`, optional).

**Rationale**: `create_entry_usecase.dart`'s own doc comment has named this extension point since RF01 shipped
("RF10 will extend this signature, never bypass it"). Positional-with-named-optional-additions is the only
shape that leaves every existing call site (`SaveTextEntryUseCase`'s and `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`'s three
manual/audio/photo sites) byte-for-byte untouched — they already call `_createEntryUseCase(content, source)`
positionally, which remains valid with the new named parameters simply omitted.

**Alternatives considered**: a parallel `CreateChatEntryUseCase` class — rejected, FR-009 explicitly wants
*one* shared interface every feature creating an entry depends on, not a second, chat-specific one that would
duplicate `CreateEntryUseCase`'s single orchestration line for no behavioral difference; making the two new
fields positional — rejected, would force every existing call site to be edited for no reason.

## R3 — `occurredAt`'s value

**Decision**: the bookmark flow always passes the originating `ChatMessage.createdAt` (the message's own send
time) as `occurredAt`, exactly as spec.md's Assumptions state ("the chat message's own `createdAt` timestamp...
not the moment the user taps the bookmark"). Every other existing caller continues to omit `occurredAt`
entirely, leaving the backend's own default (creation time = now) exactly as it behaves today for manual/
audio/photo entries — confirmed no regression, since the parameter is optional and no current caller passes
it.

**Rationale**: a bookmark can be tapped well after the message was sent (the user keeps chatting, then later
taps an earlier message's bookmark) — using "now" instead of the message's own `createdAt` would place the
resulting entry at the wrong point in the user's timeline, the exact failure mode the Assumption calls out.

## R4 — Where the bookmark's orchestration logic lives

**Decision**: `ChatBloc` gains exactly one new constructor dependency, `CreateEntryUseCase` — the sanctioned
shared seam FR-009 names directly, never `EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` — and handles the whole
bookmark flow inline via one new event (`BookmarkTapped(messageId)`) and one new private handler
(`_onBookmarkTapped`). No dedicated `SaveChatMessageUseCase`/`BookmarkRepository` class is introduced.

**Rationale**: this is the identical judgment RF04's own research.md R13 already made for every other
`ChatBloc` handler ("no extra use-case layer... every event it handles belongs to the one conversation
screen's one flow"). The bookmark handler needs exactly two calls — `CreateEntryUseCase(...)` and, on success,
`ChatRepository.recordMessageSaved(...)` — neither of which has any behavior of its own beyond what the
handler already needs inline (resolve the message by id, guard its current status, emit `saving`, await the
result, emit `saved`/`error`). A separate `BookmarkBloc` was also considered and rejected: it would either need
to duplicate `ChatBloc`'s own `messages` list (to resolve a `messageId` to its `content`/`createdAt`) or import
`ChatBloc` directly, which this codebase's established "no BLoC imports another BLoC directly" convention
(RF07's own acceptance criterion, reinforced by RF04's research.md R7) forbids.

**Alternatives considered**: a `SaveChatMessageUseCase` wrapping both calls for symmetry with `capture/`'s
use-case classes — rejected, `capture/`'s use cases exist because `InsertionModalBloc` fans out across several
structurally different tabs each needing an independently-testable "what does Save do here" unit; `ChatBloc`'s
bookmark flow has no such fan-out, so the wrapper would add a file and a DI registration with zero
testability gain over mocking `CreateEntryUseCase`/`ChatRepository` directly, the same level every other
`ChatBloc` test already mocks at.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Key Entities section is explicit that "Bookmark" is "per-message, per-viewer UI

**Alternatives considered**: as above (field on `ChatMessage`) — rejected for the reasons given; computing

1	# Quickstart: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
2	
3	How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. A run guide —
4	interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in `data-model.md`.
5	
6	## Prerequisites
7

# Quickstart: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. A run guide —
interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in `data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- RF01 and RF04 already implemented and passing — a signed-in test account can reach `/home`, send chat
  messages, and (separately) create entries via the Insertion Modal.
- At least one existing conversation with 2+ user messages, for Story 2's "save twice" and Story 4's
  "assistant has no bookmark" checks.
- A way to force a write failure for Story 3 (airplane mode toggled right before a tap, or a test double at
  the repository layer for automated tests) and, separately, a way to force an `AUTH_EXPIRED` response for the
  reauth-overlay Edge Case.
- A way to clear/forget this device's local chat cache (reinstall, or a debug-only cache-clear action) to
  exercise FR-004's "no local record of a prior success" path without needing a second physical device.

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint
fvm flutter test --coverage
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html    # RNF07 gate — bookmark_status.dart, _seedBookmarks, etc.
dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart   # ChatBloc stays within lib/features/chat/
dart test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart          # chat/domain/ imports neither Flutter nor chat/data/
```

`contracts/create-entry-usecase-chat-extension.md`, `contracts/chat-repository-bookmark-extension.md`, and
`contracts/chat-bloc-bookmark-extension.md` each carry the full scenario table this unit's coverage depends
on.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator)

### Story 1 — Turning a message you just wrote into a journal entry (P1)

1. Send a message in an active conversation. **Expect**: a bookmark control (outline icon) appears next to
   that message only, in its `idle` state.
2. Tap it. **Expect**: it shows a spinner (`saving`), then settles into an ochre check (`saved`), with no
   visible delay beyond the network round-trip.
3. Open "Meus Registros" (or wherever entries are listed). **Expect**: a new entry exists with that message's
   exact text as content, `source` = `chat`, and `chatMessageId` matching the message — structurally
   indistinguishable from any RF01-captured entry otherwise.
4. Leave the conversation (side menu → another screen) and come back, then fully restart the app and reopen
   it. **Expect**: the same message's bookmark still shows the ochre check, not reset to `idle` (FR-008).

### Story 2 — Saving the same message twice never creates a duplicate (P1)

1. On an already-`saved` bookmark, confirm it has no tap affordance at all (no visual "pressed" feedback, no
   network call fires even if tapped where the icon renders). **Expect**: exactly one entry still exists for
   that message afterward.
2. Clear/forget the device's local chat cache (or reinstall), then reopen the same conversation. **Expect**:
   the previously-saved message's bookmark renders `idle` again (the local record is gone) — tap it.
   **Expect**: it goes `saving` → `saved` again, and "Meus Registros" still shows exactly one entry for that
   message, never two (the backend's own idempotency, confirmed via `error-taxonomy.md`'s "never `409`, always
   `200`").

### Story 3 — A failed save never disrupts the conversation (P2)

1. Enable airplane mode, then tap an `idle` bookmark. **Expect**: `saving` briefly, then a red warning icon
   (`error`) — never stuck in `saving`.
2. While that bookmark is still `error`, send a new message, scroll the conversation, and tap a *different*
   message's bookmark (also while still offline, to confirm it independently reaches `error` too).
   **Expect**: every one of those actions works normally — sending still optimistically appends (and then
   itself fails/blocks per RF04's own offline behavior, unrelated to the bookmark), scrolling is unaffected,
   the second bookmark reaches its own `error` independently.
3. Disable airplane mode, then tap the first failed bookmark again. **Expect**: it re-attempts (`saving`) and
   reaches `saved`.
4. Force a session expiration (`AUTH_EXPIRED`) while a bookmark save is in flight. **Expect**: the existing
   "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the chat (Edge Cases); the bookmark itself ends in `error`
   (retryable) rather than stuck in `saving`; after re-authenticating, tapping it again succeeds normally.

### Story 4 — Only your own messages can become entries (P2)

1. In a conversation with both user and assistant messages (including at least one streaming/in-progress and
   one failed assistant response, if reachable), inspect every message. **Expect**: a bookmark control is
   present on every user message and absent from every single assistant one, with no exceptions.

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Tap a bookmark twice in rapid succession before the first tap's request resolves. **Expect**: only one
  network call fires (observable via a debug network log or a single spinner-to-settled transition, not a
  flicker of two).
- Tap the bookmark on a message the instant after sending it (before the composer's optimistic placeholder has
  been reconciled with the backend's real message id — a very narrow window, may require a slow/throttled
  connection to reliably hit). **Expect**: the tap is silently ignored; tapping again a moment later (once the
  message has a real id) works normally (research.md R6).
- A message's content at or near the entry content-length limit. **Expect**: the save either succeeds
  normally, or — if the backend's own validation rejects it — the bookmark shows `error` without crashing or
  silently dropping the attempt.
- Navigate away from a conversation while a bookmark save is in flight, then return to it. **Expect**: the
  bookmark reflects the save's actual outcome (`saved` or `error`), never a stale `saving` indicator tied to a
  request that already finished.

10	abstract class EntriesRepository {
11	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
12	    required String content,

14	  });

16	  /// FR-011's "local entries store/cache" — every entry this app has ever

9	/// timestamp below it; `failed` → "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para

This matches plan.md's scope exactly — no `records/`, `export/`, `dashboard/`, backend, or `docs/input/` files touched. No `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in this project, so there are no post-execution hooks to dispatch.

## Completion Report

Implemented P-RF10 (chat message bookmark → journal entry) per `specs/008-chat-message-bookmark/`:

**Foundational**: `BookmarkStatus` enum, two new `DesignTokens` (`sizeBookmarkIcon`, `spacingBookmarkGap`), extended `CreateEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository`/`EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`EntriesRemoteDataSource` with optional `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt`, extended `ChatRepository`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`/`ChatLocalCache` with the device-local "already saved" record (`savedEntryIdFor`/`recordMessageSaved`).

**User Story 1 (MVP)**: `BookmarkTapped` event, `ChatReady.bookmarks` map, `ChatBloc._seedBookmarks`/`_onBookmarkTapped`, new `BookmarkButton` widget (4 sub-states, matching prototype glyphs/colors), `ChatMessageBubble` extended to lay bubble+bookmark in a row for user messages only, wired into `home_chat_shell_page.dart` and DI.

**User Stories 2–4**: verification-only, as the spec anticipated — no new production code needed; added the scenario tests proving dedup, failure-isolation, and user-only placement all hold.

**Verification**: `fvm flutter analyze` clean; full suite green at 468 tests (started at 432, added 36); domain-folder coverage 93.4% (≥80% RNF07 gate); the three architecture tests (including `no_cross_feature_data_imports_test.dart`, which specifically catches a `ChatBloc` → `EntriesRepository` layer violation) all pass; `git status` confirms only the files `plan.md`'s Scale/Scope section named were touched.

The checklist gate (`checklists/bookmark.md`, 22 unchecked requirements-quality items) was flagged before starting and you chose to proceed — worth revisiting that review separately since it's unrelated to implementation completeness.
